chem_NTL.notes: Total nitrogen; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse). The total fraction, reported in every NRSA cycle, and the fraction published nitrogen criteria are written against.

chem_PH.caveat: pH carries natural geology (calcareous or naturally acidic waters) as well as disturbance, and a two-sided core narrower than measurement precision is noise rather than condition.
chem_PH.notes: pH degrades condition at BOTH extremes. Two-sided (optimum) curve: scored 1.0 across the reference interquartile core, falling in both tails.

fish_NAT_NTOLNTAX.notes: Native non-tolerant fish taxa richness (TOLERANCE_NRSA); higher is better. Total richness need not fall under disturbance, because tolerant species replace intolerant ones; this counts only the taxa that do not tolerate it.

fish_NAT_NTOLPTAX.notes: Percent of native fish taxa not classed tolerant (TOLERANCE_NRSA); higher is better. A proportion, so it does not carry the size of a region's species pool the way a richness count does.

phab_BFWD_RAT.notes: Bankfull width-to-depth ratio; both over-widened (very high) and incised (very low) degrade condition. Two-sided curve centered on the reference core.

phab_LRBS_use.notes: Log relative bed stability; departure from the reference core in EITHER direction departs from reference (negative excess fines, positive an armored, sediment-starved bed, the classic below-impoundment failure). The pilot's rising direction scored armored beds 1.0 and left Sediment continuity blind to its textbook failure mode. Two-sided form is an owner decision at the adversarial review gate, 2026-08-21.

phab_LWDeqVolM100.notes: Large woody debris volume per 100 m; higher is better.

phab_PCT_FAST.notes: Percent fast-water (riffle/run) habitat; more generally better for many biota. Ecoregion-dependent.

phab_PCT_SAFN.notes: Percent sand and fines; higher indicates fine-sediment loading (worse).

phab_SINU.notes: Channel sinuosity; higher generally indicates a more natural planform.

phab_XBKA.notes: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Direction resolved at the Northeastern Highlands review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21), consistent with the width-to-depth and bankfull-height treatment. low_tail flat added at the adversarial review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21): a regraded or naturally gentle bank holds at the Functioning edge instead of being penalized, because the flat tail is not symmetric evidence of degradation and the framework's stated use is restoration evaluation.

phab_XCDENMID.notes: Mid-channel canopy density; higher shading generally better for thermal/light regime.

phab_XCMGW.notes: Riparian canopy plus mid-layer plus ground cover; higher is better.

phab_XEMBED.notes: Percent embeddedness; higher means interstitial spaces filled with fines (worse).

phab_XFC_NAT.notes: Natural fish cover; higher is better.

bfiws.caveat: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.
bfiws.notes: Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. Moderate confidence: hydrogeology sets the baseline, so a naturally flashy till catchment reads low without being degraded (see the natural-context criterion below). Scored because flow alteration and withdrawal also move it.

DrainageAreaClass.notes: Watershed drainage area class. Breakpoints 10 and 100 km2 are fixed constants.
DrainageAreaClass.rationale: Drainage area is the primary scaling variable for channel geometry, discharge and assemblage composition. 10 km2 separates headwaters from wadeable small streams; 100 km2 separates small streams from larger wadeable rivers. Both are conventional round-number breaks in NRSA and NHDPlus practice, not sample quantiles.

ElevationClass.notes: Mean watershed elevation class. Breakpoints 300 and 1000 m are fixed constants.
ElevationClass.rationale: Elevation proxies thermal regime, precipitation phase and growing season length. 300 and 1000 m are conventional lowland, upland and montane breaks. Within a single ecoregion this often collapses to two populated classes, which the eligibility screen handles.

NhdSlopeClass.notes: NHDPlus V2 flowline slope. Adopted by the national scale analysis (rule STRAT-10).

NhdDrainageAreaClass.notes: NHDPlus V2 total drainage area. Adopted by the national scale analysis (rule STRAT-10).

precip8110ws.notes: Mean annual precipitation (1981-2010 normal); scaling/climate context, not a condition indicator. Predictor only.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 18 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 4 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 3 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

phab_XFC_NAT.methodContext: In the 10 m of channel centered on each transect, estimate the areal cover class of each fish cover type on the form (wood, brush, overhanging vegetation, undercut banks, boulders and the rest).
